passages.text: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
passages.sermon: Paul and Silas traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia.\r\nThey arrived in Thessalonica.\r\nThessalonica had a synagogue for the Jews.
passages.original: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures, explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a preacher of Jesus Christ.
Paul often visited synagogues to teach.
Paul entered the synagogue in Thessalonica.
He spoke to the people there.
He did this for three Sabbaths.
He used the Scriptures to reason with them.
He explained the meaning of the Scriptures.
He showed that the Christ had to suffer.
He proved that the Christ had to rise from the dead.
Paul said, “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ.”
passages.original: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν Χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν

passages.text: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher.
Silas was with Paul.
Paul and Silas spoke in the synagogue at Thessalonica.
Some of the Jews listened to Paul and Silas.
These Jews believed their message.
These Jews joined Paul and Silas.
Many Greeks also listened.
These Greeks respected God.
Many of these God-fearing Greeks joined Paul and Silas.
Several important women also joined Paul and Silas.
passages.original: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι

passages.text: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
passages.sermon:
Some Jews became jealous.
They brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace.
These men were evil.
The Jews formed a mob with them.
They caused an uproar in the city.
They went to Jason’s house.
They searched for Paul and Silas there.
They wanted to bring Paul and Silas out to the people.
passages.original: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον

passages.text: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here, and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
passages.sermon:
The Jews could not find Paul and Silas.
They seized Jason and some other brothers.
They dragged Jason and the others to the city officials.
They shouted loudly before the officials.
They said, “These men have turned the world upside down.
Now they have come here too.
Jason has welcomed them into his home.
All these men act against Caesar’s decrees.
They say there is another king.
They say this king is Jesus.”
passages.original: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσι βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
passages.sermon:
The crowd heard these accusations.
The city officials also heard them.
The crowd became greatly disturbed.
The city officials also became greatly disturbed.
passages.original: Ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα

passages.text: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.
passages.sermon: The city officials took money from Jason and the others as a bond.\r\nThey accepted this payment.\r\nThen the city officials released Jason and the others.
passages.original: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς

passages.text: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
passages.sermon:
The brothers acted quickly at night.
They sent Paul and Silas away to Berea.
Paul and Silas arrived in Berea.
They went into the Jewish synagogue.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν

passages.text: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
passages.sermon:
The Bereans lived in the city of Berea.
The Bereans had a noble character.
The Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians.
The Bereans received the message with great eagerness.
The Bereans examined the Scriptures every day.
The Bereans wanted to see if these teachings were true.
passages.original: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως

passages.text: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
passages.sermon: Many Bereans believed the message.\r\nMany prominent Greek women also believed.\r\nMany Greek men believed as well.
passages.original: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι

passages.text: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
passages.sermon:
The Jews from Thessalonica heard news about Paul.
They learned that Paul was preaching the word of God in Berea.
These Jews traveled to Berea.
They stirred up the crowds in Berea.
They caused trouble among the people there.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους

passages.text: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian preacher.
The brothers acted quickly.
They sent Paul away at once.
They sent him to the coast.
Silas stayed in Berea.
Timothy also stayed in Berea.
passages.original: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ

passages.text: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian missionary and apostle.
Some men escorted Paul.
They brought Paul to Athens.
These men received instructions for Silas and Timothy.
The instructions told Silas and Timothy to come to Paul as soon as possible.
The men left Athens and returned with these instructions.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν

passages.text: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
passages.sermon: Paul waited for Silas and Timothy in Athens.\r\nPaul saw that the city was full of idols.\r\nPaul felt deeply disturbed in his spirit.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν

passages.text: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
passages.sermon:
Paul was in Athens.
Paul waited for Silas and Timothy.
Paul spoke with people every day.
He went to the synagogue.
He talked with the Jews there.
He also talked with God-fearing Gentiles there.
He went to the marketplace each day.
He spoke with anyone he met in the marketplace.
passages.original: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας

passages.text: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
passages.sermon:
Some Epicurean philosophers began to debate with Paul.
Some Stoic philosophers also debated with Paul.
Some of these philosophers asked a question.
They said, “What is this babbler trying to say?”
Other philosophers made a different statement.
They said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.”
Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus.
Paul was also proclaiming the resurrection.
This is why they said he was advocating foreign gods.
passages.original: Τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρείων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ καί τινες ἔλεγον Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν οἱ δέ Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο

passages.text: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
passages.sermon:
Some men took Paul.
They brought Paul to the Areopagus.
The Areopagus was a place in Athens where people discussed new ideas.
These men spoke to Paul.
They asked Paul a question.
They said, “May we know what this new teaching is?”
They said, “You are presenting this teaching to us.”
passages.original: Ἐπιλαβόμενοί τε αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον πάγον ἤγαγον λέγοντες Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή

passages.text: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
passages.sermon:
The people in Athens loved to discuss new ideas.
They often listened to new teachings.
They said to Paul, “You are bringing strange ideas to us.”
They wanted to understand these new ideas.
They asked Paul what these things meant.
passages.original: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι

passages.text: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
passages.sermon:
The people of Athens loved new ideas.
Foreigners who lived in Athens also loved new ideas.
They spent their time talking about new things.
They also spent their time listening to new things.
They did not spend their time on anything else.
passages.original: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον

passages.text: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus.
The Areopagus was a meeting place in Athens.
Paul spoke to the people gathered there.
He addressed the men of Athens.
Paul said, "Men of Athens, I see something about you."
He said, "In every way, you are very religious."
Paul noticed their religious practices and beliefs.
He recognized that the Athenians showed great devotion to spiritual matters.
passages.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ

passages.text: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people of Athens.
Paul walked around their city.
Paul looked carefully at their objects of worship.
Paul saw many things that the people honored.
Paul found an altar.
The altar had an inscription.
The inscription said, “To an Unknown God.”
The people of Athens worshiped something they did not know.
Paul told them about this unknown God.
Paul proclaimed the truth about this God to them.
passages.original: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ Ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν

passages.text: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
passages.sermon:
God made the world.
God made everything in the world.
God is the Lord of heaven.
God is the Lord of earth.
God does not live in temples.
People make temples with their hands.
God does not live in temples made by people.
passages.original: Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων Κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ

passages.text: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
passages.sermon:
God does not need anything from people.
People do not serve God with their hands as if He needed help.
God gives life to everyone.
God gives breath to everyone.
God gives everything to everyone.
passages.original: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα

passages.text: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
passages.sermon:
God made every nation of people.
God made all these nations from one man.
God wanted people to live on the whole earth.
God decided when each nation would exist.
God set the boundaries where each nation would live.
passages.original: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
passages.sermon:
God created every nation from one man.
God determined where and when each nation would live.
God did this so that people would seek Him.
God wants people to reach out for Him.
God wants people to find Him.
God is not far from any one of us.
passages.original: ζητεῖν τὸν Θεὸν εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα

passages.text: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God gives us life.
We live in God.
We move in God.
We exist because of God.
Some of your own poets have said this.
They said, “We are His offspring.”
We are God’s children.
passages.original: Ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν

passages.text: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
passages.sermon:
We are God’s offspring.
God made us.
We should not think that God is like gold.
We should not think that God is like silver.
We should not think that God is like stone.
People make images from gold, silver, or stone.
People use their skill and imagination to make these images.
God is not like any image made by people.
passages.original: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου τὸ Θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον

passages.text: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator and Father of all people.
God overlooked the ignorance of people in earlier times.
Now God commands every person to repent.
God gives this command to all people everywhere.
passages.original: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ νῦν παραγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν

passages.text: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
passages.sermon:
God has set a specific day.
On that day, God will judge the whole world.
God will judge with justice.
God will use a certain Man to judge.
God Himself has chosen this Man.
God has given proof to everyone about this Man.
God raised this Man from the dead.
passages.original: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke about the resurrection of the dead.
Some people listened to Paul.
Some people mocked Paul when they heard about the resurrection.
Other people spoke to Paul.
They said, “We want to hear you again about this topic.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν

passages.text: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
passages.sermon: Paul was at the Areopagus.\r\nPaul left the people there.\r\nPaul went away from the Areopagus.
passages.original: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν

passages.text: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
passages.sermon:
Some men joined Paul.
They believed his message.
Dionysius was one of them.
Dionysius was an Areopagite.
A woman named Damaris also joined Paul.
Other people joined them as well.
passages.original: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς
